text:
maria: ran a quick nsys + perfetto sweep on the 2.1.0-serving build, seeing a weird long tail of tiny kernels that add up. attaching top-level summary and a perfetto link. anyone else seeing this on reg branches?

jonathan: can you paste the nsys top-kernel dump? curious about total vs avg time.

maria: sure — gist of the nsys summary i pulled (shortened):
```
# nsys summary (1800203345)
Top kernels by total wall time
1  attention_compute_fwd         41.9%   1.18s
2  fused_gemm_kv                 19.2%   0.54s
3  kv_prefetch_small             13.1%   0.37s
4  softmax_dropout               6.3%    0.18s
5  launch_overhead               4.6%    0.13s
# note: kv_prefetch_small has ~4k launches, avg 90us
```
perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/REDWOOD/abcd1234 (nsys->perfetto export)

lee: 4k launches for one kernel screams batching/heuristic issue. could be our new batching cutoff that tried to reduce latency for small seqs — ended up fragmenting the KV prefetch.

sam: we rolled the batching threshold change in canary yesterday (PR #4123). it grouped short requests aggressively but i thought it would coalesce kv prefetches, not fragment them. did you test with kv-cache enabled?

maria: kv-cache = on. the behavior looks like: requests with short context cause repeated kv_prefetch_small kernels rather than one bigger prefetch. that increases kernel launch overhead and hurts SM utilization.

jonathan: can you check occupancy and SM util per-kernel? NVPROF/nsight data helps. small kernels often have low occupancy and high per-launch cost.

maria: grabbed a quick occupancy snapshot from nsight:
```
# nsight per-kernel (sample)
attention_compute_fwd: occupancy 78%  (good), avg SM util 65%
fused_gemm_kv: occupancy 62%, avg SM util 51%
kv_prefetch_small: occupancy 18%, avg SM util 12%  <-- bad
launch_overhead: n/a (driver)
```

lee: yep, kv_prefetch_small is the suspect. low occupancy + many launches = wasted cycles. options: increase coalesce window, switch to async prefetch with single larger kernel, or fuse prefetch into attention pipeline.

sam: quick experiment idea: bump batching coalesce window from 3ms -> 8ms for the small-seq path and re-run nsys. should reduce number of prefetch kernels by grouping nearby requests. downside: small latency increase for p95.

maria: ran a micro with the coalesce window at 8ms on canary (build b437). results: kv_prefetch_small launches dropped from ~4k -> ~900, total prefetch time down 60%, but p95 token latency up ~6ms.

jonathan: that's promising. can you also try a fused prefetch kernel (one kernel that loops over N entries) to improve occupancy? fusion usually improves occupancy for memory-bound ops.

maria: i have a prototype fused kernel (local branch). fused run shows kv_prefetch (fused) occupancy 46% and total time down another 25% vs the coalesce-change. p95 latency similar to coalesce.

perf-bot: automated note — regression check between 2.0.9 and 2.1.0-serving: attention_compute_fwd stable, kv-prefetch-related wall time increased by 28% on average workloads. See /perf/regressions/1800203345.

lee: TL;DR we have two knobs: runtime batching/coalesce and kernel fusion. Both reduce launch count; fusion also boosts occupancy. tradeoffs: coalesce = easier, latency reg; fusion = dev time + memory tradeoffs.

sam: for rollout plan i'd do: 1) revert aggressive cutoff in canary or set coalesce to 8ms, 2) roll fused prefetch as opt-in behind config, 3) monitor p95 and token cost for next 48h.

maria: agreed. i'll open an action thread with the numbers and the perfetto link + nsight screenshots. also adding a short reproducer script to run in CI:
```bash
# repro quick-run
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --trace=nvtx,cuda --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi \
  --sample=all --stop-on-exit python -m tests.perf.run_small_seq_load
```

jonathan: nice. add a flag to run both fused and unfused so we can A/B in CI. cc @lee for kernel review.

deploy-bot: canary build b437 deployed to cluster-alpha at 2026-03-17T14:02:00Z (for testing).

lee: i'll review the fused kernel tomorrow morning, pls attach the branch. if it looks good we'll gate it behind feature flag and get perf-signoff. :thumbsup:

maria: filed issue RD-INF-1284 with attachments (nsys summaries, perfetto link, prototype branch). assigning to @lee and @sam. thanks all. :slightly_smiling_face:
